text:
Sam_CE: heads-up — AcmeMobile just opened a P0. Customers seeing intermittent 503s on /v1/generate (hosted). SLA hit window is tomorrow EOD PST if not mitigated. stacktrace + request ids in the ticket. :warning:
Maria_EP: acknowledged. can you paste one example request_id and the approximate spike window?
Sam_CE: request_id: rq_20231107_9f3b. Spike started ~09:12 PDT, 09:12–09:28 had ~30% error rate, then dropped but still elevated. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-4521
Priya_SRE: @Maria_EP @Liang_RT tagging for hot triage. Is this a model-serving OOM / node restart pattern or a routing spike?
Liang_RT: looking at runtime logs now. early signs point to an autoscale mis-slope on pool-12 (dedicated) — nodes are entering drain and not rejoining fast enough. seeing KV-cache warm failures ~09:13.
Maria_EP: ok can you confirm whether fallback to the cpu-quantized model would avoid the path that hits the failing instance? If yes, we can flip routing while we debug.
Liang_RT: quick check: fallback candidate exists (models/redwood-small-q4f32). latency will increase ~120–200ms but should reduce 503s. Need a manual routing override to test.
Nate_PM: +1 to fallback test. Communicate customer impact and duration if we do it. OpsBot: deploy canary job queued by @Maria_EP.
Maria_EP: I'll run a manual routing override to route 20% traffic to the fallback for 10 minutes, then increase if stable. Doing it now: /api/admin/route-override --pool pool-12 --to redwood-small-q4f32 --pct 20 --ttl 10m
OpsBot: job started (job_id: jb_9342). Check logs at /console/overrides/jb_9342. :gear:
Priya_SRE: monitoring: error-rate drop visible at 09:18 as override rolls out. sending customer update now.
Sam_CE: sending update: "We enabled a safe fallback to a compatible model to reduce errors. We expect a temporary latency increase; service continuity is priority. Investigating root cause — will follow up with timeline." :thumbsup:
Liang_RT: digging deeper — node drain initiated by a flaky NVIDIA driver update from last night's image roll (image: rw-gpu-2026-03-16). Repro steps: forced restart of one node triggers driver timeout -> kubelet drains -> fail to re-register due to missing nvidia driver probe.
Priya_SRE: rollback plan: we can roll the image back on pool-12 to rw-gpu-2026-03-14 which is stable. But that requires a coordinated rolling restart and will take ~25–35 minutes for pool.
Maria_EP: decision? fallback is live and stable at 20%. Recommend: continue to 50% for next 15m, then start image rollback if no regression. Who owns the rollback? @Priya_SRE to coordinate with infra. @Liang_RT to validate kernel/driver fixes post-rollback.
Priya_SRE: I own rollback. ETA to start: 10m (waiting on approvals). I'll post a runbook here and ping infra.
Nate_PM: I'll update the account and offer an incident bridge for any escalation. Good call on the fallback.
Sam_CE: thanks everyone — please post status updates here. will escalate to SEs after the rollback if customers still see issues. :pray:
Maria_EP: update: increased override to 50% at 09:26. error-rate down to baseline (~1.2%). Proceeding with rollback at 09:35.
OpsBot: rollback job started (job_id: rb_1108). Rolling restarts across pool-12 nodes.
Priya_SRE: running rollback, tracking in ops doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ops/pool-12-rollback. Will post when complete.
Liang_RT: post-rollback validation plan: smoke test /v1/generate across 5 regions, check KV warm success count, confirm pods re-register within 60s.
Sam_CE: customer notified: next update in 30m or after rollback completes. thanks all.
Maria_EP: final note — we should add an autoscale policy tweak to prevent aggressive drains during image mismatches. Filing follow-up ticket RW-4537.
Priya_SRE: rollback complete at 10:02. pods rejoined, driver probe passing. error-rate stable. closing P0 if no regressions in 1h.
Sam_CE: closing loop with customer now. great work team. :tada:
